_strings.@@698bfa61e0cd: Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit — Montana residents age 62 or older as of December 31, 2023, who lived in Montana at least 9 months during the tax year, occupied a Montana residence as a renter, owner, or lessee for at least 6 months during the year, and whose total gross household income (all household members) is under the limit. _strings.@@a51fb3ae9eac: Treaty conformity — MT conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MT income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MT return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: MT conforms. For tax year 2023, the Montana Form 2 instructions state plainly: "Your income on your Montana tax return begins with your Federal Adjusted Gross Income" (2023 Form 2 Instructions, "Federal Adjusted Gross Income" section, p.9). Federally treaty-exempt income (excluded from federal AGI under an applicable U.S. tax treaty) is therefore already absent from the MT starting figure. The Montana Additions Schedule defines additions as "all items of income that are not included in Federal Adjusted Gross Income and that must be added" (p.10/p.17), and its enumerated lines are: Line 1 Recovery of Federal Income Tax Deducted; Line 2 Other Recoveries; Line 5 Smaller Federal Estate/Trust Distributions; Line 6 Medical Savings Account nonqualified withdrawals; Line 7 First-Time Home-Buyer Account nonqualified withdrawals; Line 9 Federal Net Operating Loss Deduction; Line 10 Expenses used to claim a MT credit; Line 11 Farm/Ranch Risk Management distributions; Line 12 pass-through entity (K-1) additions; Line 13 Title Plant Depreciation/Amortization; Line 14 State Income Tax Deduction; Line 15 Other Additions. NONE is an add-back of treaty-exempt income. Line 15 ("Other Additions") examples are limited to passive/rental and capital loss carryover differences and uncredited S-corp federal income tax — not treaty income. Unlike California (Schedule CA), Montana has no treaty-income addback for 2023, so treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed.

_strings.@@b7715a31b250: There is no separate nonresident/part-year individual form for 2023. Nonresidents and part-year residents also file Montana Form 2, and additionally complete the Nonresident/Part-Year Resident Ratio Schedule (Form 2, page 8) to apportion the tax. (The DER-1 referenced in the instructions is for single-member LLCs owned by nonresidents, not the individual return.)
_strings.@@e4f9aea3d6b9: Credit for Income Tax Paid to Another State or Country — Full-year or part-year Montana residents who paid income tax to another state or country on an item of income that is also included in their Montana Adjusted Gross Income while a Montana resident. Penalties and interest paid to the other state/country are excluded; a separate schedule must be completed for each state/country.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 2, page 1, line 18 'Tax liability before credits (See instructions)'. Instructions p.11: 'Residents: If you are a full-year resident, and you owe neither any recapture tax (see page 37), nor any taxes on lump-sum distributions (see page 39), compute your tax using the following table and report the result on line 18.' The table is keyed to 'your taxable income (page 1, line 17)' (Form 2, page 8, Tax Liability Schedule line 1 / line 6 'Resident tax'). This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2023 Montana Form 2, page 1, line 17 — 'Taxable income. Subtract lines 15 and 16 from line 14. If zero or less, enter 0.' Compute it on the form: line 11 federal AGI (from federal Form 1040) + line 12 Montana additions - line 13 Montana subtractions = line 14 Montana Adjusted Gross Income; then subtract line 15 standard or itemized deductions (standard deduction = 20% of line 14, capped at $5,540 single/MFS or $11,080 MFJ/HoH and floored at $2,460 single/MFS or $4,920 MFJ/HoH — income-dependent, so this op does NOT subtract it) and line 16 exemptions ($2,960 x total exemptions from the Exemptions Section line d). The op subtracts NOTHING further — line 17 already reflects all deductions and exemptions. ONE rate schedule for ALL filing statuses: the 2023 Montana tax table (Form 2, page 8; instructions p.11) does not vary by filing status — Single, Married Filing Jointly, Married Filing Separately, and Head of Household all use the identical seven-bracket schedule, duplicated per status here. 2023 Form 2 has NO qualifying-surviving-spouse filing status (statuses printed on the form: 1 Single, 2a Married filing separately on the same form, 2b Married filing separately on separate forms, 2c Married filing separately and spouse not filing, 3 Head of household, 4 Married filing jointly); the engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping is numerically harmless because one schedule covers every status. Federal-conformed filing statuses (including qualifying widower) arrive only in Tax Year 2024. The printed 'And Subtract' constants ($0/$36/$99/$196/$326/$496... precisely $36, $99, $196, $326, $494, $656) equal the cumulative sum of the prior brackets EXACTLY — no rounding divergence. The form's own example ($25,000 taxable income -> $25,000 x 6.75% = $1,688; $1,688 - $656 = $1,032) matches marginal bracket math with half-up rounding ($1,031.50 -> $1,032). STANDARD DEDUCTION NOT SHIPPED (income-dependent): Montana's 2023 standard deduction is 20% of Montana Adjusted Gross Income (Form 2, line 14), capped at a MAXIMUM of $5,540 (single or married filing separately) / $11,080 (married filing jointly or head of household) and floored at a MINIMUM of $2,460 (single/MFS) / $4,920 (MFJ/HoH) — Standard Deduction Worksheet, Form 2, page 7. Compute line 15 on the form (or use itemized deductions — Montana's itemized schedule allows federal income tax paid, among other items). Supply line 17, which already reflects line 15. EXEMPTIONS NOT SHIPPED (already inside line 17): Form 2, line 16 = $2,960 x total exemptions from the Exemptions Section, line d — one for yourself, one for your spouse, one per dependent, PLUS one ADDITIONAL exemption for each '65 or older' checkbox and each 'Blind' checkbox (taxpayer and spouse). Because the caller supplies line 17 taxable income, the op must not subtract exemptions again. Resident Capital Gains Credit is a CREDIT, not a base reduction: 2% of net capital gains reported on Form 2, line 7, claimed on the Nonrefundable Credits Schedule line 1 and subtracted from tax at Form 2, line 19 — NOT modeled by this op. Montana Earned Income Tax Credit (Form 2, line 23b = 3% of the federal EITC) is a refundable CREDIT — NOT modeled by this op. Recapture taxes (e.g., the 6.75% Medical Savings Account / First-Time Home Buyer Account recapture) and the tax on lump-sum distributions (federal Form 4972) are ADDED to line 18 via the Tax Liability Schedule (Form 2, page 8, lines 2 and 4) — NOT modeled; if owed, line 18 exceeds plain bracket math on line 17. Nonresidents and part-year residents: bracket math on line 17 yields only Tax Liability Schedule line 1; the tax is then MULTIPLIED by the Montana-source ratio (Form 2, page 8, lines 3a or 5, ratio from the Nonresident/Part-Year Resident Ratio Schedule). This op models the full-year RESIDENT computation (Tax Liability Schedule line 6 with no recapture or lump-sum tax). Married filing separately on the same form (status 2a): each spouse computes their own tax in their own column (Columns A and B) — apply this op once per spouse, each using that spouse's own line 17 taxable income. No lookup-table mandate: Montana prints a rate FORMULA schedule ('Multiply Your Taxable Income By ... And Subtract'), not a row-lookup tax table, so bracket math is exact at every income level. 2023 is the FINAL year of this structure and there was NO mid-year 2023 rate change: under SB 399 (2021) and SB 121 (2023), beginning Tax Year 2024 Montana starts from federal TAXABLE income, drops the Montana standard deduction and exemptions, and condenses to two rates (4.7% / 5.9%; the 6.75% top rate ends after 2023). Do not use this pack for tax year 2024.
